title: BYO corpus record — google_drive
description: A Google Drive file. Content is returned by files.export; subtype picks the Workspace type / export format.

content.description: The retrieval payload served verbatim as the body.

title.description: Document title (email subject / file name / issue title / page title).

folder.description: The folder this document belongs to.

group.description: ACL group owning the folder (default: slug(container)); null means the container owns no group, so nothing is group-scoped to it.

author_name.description: The owner's display name as the corpus writes it, served as the document's owner (a name is not recoverable from an email address).

visibility.description: public = org-wide, group = the container's group, private = author only.

readers.description: Explicit reader principals. `user:<email>` / `group:<id>` / `org:<name>` state the type; unprefixed, an address is a user and anything else a group. Overrides visibility — and an EMPTY array means nobody may read the document (admin-only), not everybody.

subtype.description: Drive file type (default: document). The four Workspace native types (`document`/`spreadsheet`/`presentation`/`folder`) get a `application/vnd.google-apps.*` mimeType and an /edit link; every other value is a binary file kind whose mimeType comes from `mime_type`, or from the value itself when it names a known extension.

sheets.description: A real grid, for a `spreadsheet`. Authoritative when present, and then `content` must be ABSENT: content is derived from the FIRST sheet at import, so a record stating both would let Drive search find words no cell holds. The same derivation is why Drive's full-text search reaches only the first sheet -- a word held on a later one is in no cell `content` carries, so `files.list?q=fullText contains` will not find the file by it. Omit `sheets` and `content` keeps its meaning unchanged -- one sheet whose every cell is a whole line of it.

title.description: Sheet name (default: `Sheet<n>` by position). Unique within the workbook, compared case-insensitively.

grid.description: Rows of cells. A cell is a JSON scalar -- a string, a number, a boolean, or null for an empty cell -- so the type the corpus states is the type the API serves. Short rows are padded at import. An empty array is an empty sheet, which a workbook really has; a row with no cells at all (`[[]]`) is a typo rather than a shape a corpus means, so `minItems` refuses it.

paragraphs.description: The document's paragraphs, for a `document`, each with its named style and its runs of text, so the Docs API serves the headings, bold, italic and links a document really has. Authoritative when present, and then `content` must be ABSENT: it is derived at import as the paragraphs' text, one line each, which Drive's export and full-text search read. Omit `paragraphs` and `content` keeps its meaning unchanged -- one plain paragraph per line of it.

text.description: The paragraph's text, unstyled and without its newline. An empty string is an empty paragraph. State this or `runs`, not both. No character real strips from a document's text (U+0000-U+0008, U+000C-U+001F, U+E000-U+F8FF) and none `insertText` refuses (U+FDD0-U+FDEF).

runs.description: The paragraph's text as runs, each with the marks it carries, in order and without the paragraph's newline. State this or `text`, not both.

link.description: The URL the run links to, starting with a scheme: text before its first `:` with no `.`, `/`, `?` or `#` in it (`https:`, `mailto:`). Real stores most other values as an `http://` URL, `wiki.acme.example:8443/page` among them, and a `#heading=` value as a heading link, so a document holds neither as stated. A link is served underlined and in the link colour, as the editor makes one.
